{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history includes positive values (e.g., >0.00), indicating bullish bias that often overestimates prices.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when historical price patterns show mean reversion toward prior 15-day average.",
    "If model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >10% above recent 15-day high), apply a 5-10% downward correction to prevent overshoot.",
    "When true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by >5% over 3 consecutive days, apply a 2-3% downward bias correction to align with mean reversion.",
    "For sentiment history with 0.00, assume neutral market; use 15-day moving average as baseline, with ±3% tolerance band for volatility.",
    "If forecast is below 60% of 15-day high for 3+ consecutive days, consider upward bias correction to avoid underestimating rebound potential.",
    "In cases where true outcome exceeds forecast by >15% and sentiment is neutral, apply a 5% upward adjustment to account for lagged market reaction."
  ]
}
